title: Cross-session FUSE persistence investigation: tinker's 2026-07-18 run reported FUSE missing 6 days of tinker report-*.json files (07-12 through 07-17) despite dome-mirror running successfully every day. Diagnose whether scheduled-agent FUSE mounts share persistent state, and if not, recommend the routing pattern.

context.why_now: Tinker's 2026-07-18T02:40Z summary flagged a housekeeping finding directly to operator: FUSE workspace was missing six days of prior tinker reports (2026-07-12 through 2026-07-17). Tinker verified via a fresh clone that git had all six reports fine, and pushed today's outputs through the clone-based path so they're not dependent on FUSE sync timing. This is not a data-loss incident — nothing was lost. But it exposes an unresolved question about how scheduled-agent FUSE mounts interact with each other.

what_is_demonstrably_true_no_speculation.dome_mirror_was_running: Sentinels exist in monitor/integrity/sync-workspace-runs-*.json for every day 2026-07-08 through 2026-07-18, three per day (00:35 / 04:35 / 08:35 UTC). No gap in dome-mirror's scheduled runs.
what_is_demonstrably_true_no_speculation.sync_script_reported_success: Latest sentinel (2026-07-18T08-34-59Z) shows classification=equal, files_copied=116, new_files=5, sync_exit_code=0, upstream_newer_than_last_sync=true. dome-mirror's script successfully invoked build.js sync-workspace and it copied files.
what_is_demonstrably_true_no_speculation.ownership_routes_report_files_correctly: monitor/tinker/ is classified 'append_only_glob' in build.js OWNERSHIP. syncToWorkspace's walkAppendOnly branch recursively copies files from git to FUSE when they don't already exist in FUSE. Code path is correct.
what_is_demonstrably_true_no_speculation.the_reports_were_in_git: Fresh clone (git HEAD) had all six reports 07-12 through 07-17 with correct timestamps and content. Tinker confirmed.

context.the_operator_working_hypothesis_unverifi: Scheduled agent sessions may have per-session FUSE mounts that don't share state cleanly with subsequent scheduled sessions. Dome-mirror writes into its session's mount, session ends, and the next scheduled session (e.g., tinker's later run) starts from a fresh FUSE snapshot that doesn't reflect dome-mirror's writes. Same architectural theme as DIRECTIVE-20260708-001's EPERM finding (per-session FUSE mounts with deny-by-default unlink) — the scheduled-session FUSE has isolation properties that don't match the 'shared persistent workspace' mental model the pipeline was designed around.
context.why_this_matters: If the working hypothesis is correct, dome-mirror's git→FUSE work is largely ineffective for cross-session propagation to scheduled agents. Its writes evaporate at session-end. This would mean the 'FUSE workspace' as-designed is really a per-session workspace for scheduled agents, and any cross-session sharing depends on git as the shared substrate. Every agent that reads its own prior outputs (or another agent's prior outputs) would need to read from a fresh clone, not FUSE — the PROP-135 pattern extended.
context.why_operator_cowork_doesnt_see_this_clas: The Cowork FUSE at /sessions/<cowork-session>/mnt/dome-model-review/ persists across the operator's interactions with Claude — it's warm across the entire conversation. Scheduled agent sessions get fresh sandboxes on each firing. Whatever cross-session persistence the platform provides, it's imperfect for scheduled contexts.

part_A_observational_diagnosis.why_first: Cheaper than experimental probe. Use existing sentinel + git-log data to determine whether the working hypothesis is supported.
questions_to_answer: Q1 — When dome-mirror's sentinel reports files_copied=N and new_files=K for a given day, does a LATER scheduled session (from a different agent, say tinker or integrity that runs after dome-mirror) actually see those N+K files in its own FUSE view when it runs? Look at each scheduled agent's run logs or self-cost outputs — did they read files that dome-mirror had just copied 'to FUSE', or did they clone-based read from git?

Q2 — Is there any evidence that scheduled sessions share FUSE state successfully? Check whether any agent writes to FUSE and a later scheduled agent reads from that exact FUSE-written state (as opposed to reading from git via clone).

Q3 — Look at the specific 6-day gap tinker observed: for 07-12 through 07-17, do dome-mirror's sentinels for those days claim to have copied the corresponding tinker report-*.json files (or claim they were already present)? If dome-mirror's script claims success but tinker's FUSE didn't have them, that quantifies the gap.

Q4 — Are there prior tinker reports (before 07-12) that DID make it to FUSE somehow? If yes, when did they arrive, from what agent/session, and via what mechanism? This bounds when the class of failure began.
part_A_observational_diagnosis.investigation_scope: Read-only. Analyze sentinels + git log + prior tinker reports' file-presence signals. Do NOT write probe files, do NOT modify scheduled tasks, do NOT modify sync-workspace-step4c.js. If a probe is needed, propose it in Part C for operator authorization.
part_A_observational_diagnosis.output: monitor/tinker/reports/cross-session-fuse-persistence-diagnosis-2026-07-18.md — 1-2 page report answering Q1-Q4 with sentinel + commit evidence.

options_to_consider.label: Extend PROP-135 clone-based-read discipline to all agents that read prior agent outputs
options_to_consider.shape: Codify in the relevant prompt files (tinker.md, analyst.md, curmudgeon.md, decider.md, etc.) that reads of 'prior agent outputs' (report-*.json, review files, EXPs, priority-queue, etc.) MUST come from a fresh clone, not FUSE. Small prompt edits. Same discipline PROP-135 shipped for status.json applied more broadly.
options_to_consider.cost: Small — prompt edits across N agents. No code changes.
options_to_consider.risk: Low. Agents already clone fresh; this just requires them to also READ from clone rather than reaching into FUSE.

options_to_consider.label: Accept the cross-session FUSE gap as documented steady state
options_to_consider.shape: Add a CLAUDE.md addendum documenting the observation. Note the workaround (clone-based read) for anyone hitting the class in the future.
options_to_consider.risk: The class recurs whenever an agent forgets to clone-read. Some rate of housekeeping-finding surfacings continues.

options_to_consider.label: Design a probe (experimental) to definitively confirm/refute the hypothesis
options_to_consider.shape: A scheduled task fires agent-A, which writes a marker file to FUSE with a known unique payload. N minutes later, scheduled task fires agent-B, which reads the marker file from FUSE and reports whether it was found. Iterate across different agent combinations and time gaps.
options_to_consider.cost: Moderate — new probe scheduled task + coordination code.
options_to_consider.risk: Low. Probe files are inert. The scheduled-task infrastructure exists.

options_to_consider.label: Investigate whether platform-side FUSE persistence can be configured differently
options_to_consider.shape: Out of scope for tinker — this would require operator escalation to Anthropic support / platform team. Note in the report if the observational diagnosis suggests this class of change is warranted.
options_to_consider.cost: N/A — tinker doesn't act on this option; it just flags it for operator.

part_B_recommendation.output: One-paragraph recommendation. Explicit acceptance of OPT-2 (do nothing structural, document + accept) as legitimate outcome if the hypothesis check goes against the working hypothesis (i.e., FUSE persistence IS working but something else caused the 6-day gap).

part_C_ship_or_defer.if_OPT_1_is_small: Ship in the same run as small prompt edits + a PROP documenting the discipline.
part_C_ship_or_defer.if_OPT_2: Ship the CLAUDE.md addendum, close directive.
part_C_ship_or_defer.if_OPT_3: Design the probe in a follow-up PROP + operator ratifies before running.
part_C_ship_or_defer.if_hypothesis_refuted: The observational diagnosis may show the working hypothesis was wrong. In that case, report what actually happened + propose the corresponding fix or close as 'unable to root-cause from observational data' with a specific request for probe.

deliverable_acceptance_criteria: monitor/tinker/reports/cross-session-fuse-persistence-diagnosis-2026-07-18.md — 1-2 page report answering Q1-Q4 with concrete sentinel + commit evidence.
One PROP or CLAUDE.md addendum implementing the recommended option (OPT-1 / OPT-2 / OPT-3-design).
If OPT-1 is chosen, the PROP includes the specific prompt edits per agent, with fixture verification.
If OPT-2 is chosen, the CLAUDE.md addendum documents the observed class + the clone-based-read workaround pattern.

If OPT-3 is chosen, the probe design PROP includes: (a) scheduled task cron for probe firing, (b) marker file format + unique-payload discipline, (c) reader script + report format, (d) fail-safe (probe files auto-expire, don't accumulate).

constraints.no_production_agent_changes_in_this_dire: Investigate + recommend. Any prompt edits (OPT-1) or CLAUDE.md addendum (OPT-2) or probe design (OPT-3) is a SEPARATE deliverable. This directive is about the diagnosis first; the ship comes second.
constraints.no_speculation_beyond_evidence: Tinker's report should state what the sentinels + commits + prior-report file-presence data can support. Where the evidence doesn't reach, say so — do not invent architectural details about scheduled-agent FUSE that aren't observable.
constraints.prop_051_awareness_for_OPT_1: If OPT-1 ships prompt edits touching how agents read state, ensure the edits don't accidentally introduce a new class of race (e.g., clone-based reads that miss FUSE-side workspace-owned state). Reference the PROP-135 pattern's field-merge discipline as the model.
constraints.do_not_modify_dome_mirror: dome-mirror's script is working as-specified. The gap is architectural, not a script bug. Any recommendation that involves modifying sync-workspace-step4c.js needs a separate directive with clear rationale.
